clue.text: Key aide: very few could afford one with forty-eight hours off

indicators.note: to afford is to yield or produce, as in affording an opportunity, so these letters are made to yield a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
V is the standard abbreviation for very
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trusted assistant rarely gets a two-day break from the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pushes you towards an overworked assistant, but the first three words plus V are the letters to rework. Forty-eight hours off is the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: A working week of Monday to Friday leaves Saturday and Sunday, two whole days, free from employment.

clue.text: Delivers one a plant

parts.note: to deliver someone is to set them free
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a single flowering plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivers' reads like handing over a parcel, but here it means liberates, as in 'deliver us from evil'.
explanation.definitionFit: The freesia is a sweet-scented flowering bulb from southern Africa, popular in bouquets and gardens.

clue.text: One bowed out of awkward love-in with cool Liberal

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of place, so these letters sit badly and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Someone takes a bow and slips away from an embarrassing hippie gathering with a laid-back politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bowed' sounds like a person who took a bow, but it means an instrument played with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The violoncello, usually shortened to cello, is a large string instrument sounded by drawing a bow across it.

clue.text: Ready to roll?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 'the ready' is British slang for cash

definitions.note: read as 'something to roll', a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a baker rolls out flat with a pin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready to roll' reads as one phrase, set to go; split it, and 'ready' is British slang for money while the rest describes pastry mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word for cash is also unbaked mixture of flour and water, which is what bakers flatten with a pin.

clue.text: TV show you and son prepare to attend

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
S is the abbreviation for son
to prime something is to get it ready
to minister to someone is to attend to their needs

explanation.surface: A television programme in which a parent and child get ready to go along.
explanation.walkthrough: The breaks fall differently in the answer: YE and S join to make the first word. The show is a 1980s BBC sitcom about a prime minister and his civil servants.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a celebrated British television comedy series about a prime minister outwitted by his officials.

clue.text: Nymph looked back on chance with regret, reflecting over years

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so these letters are turned back to front

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Y is the abbreviation for years
dice are the classic instruments of chance

explanation.surface: Someone looks back regretfully over the years at the chances they took.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the reversed piece above Y, and 'on' places all that above DICE. In Greek myth Orpheus lost her by looking back as he led her out of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the wood nymph whom Orpheus fatally glanced behind at while leading her up from Hades.

clue.text: Make awkward progress on a graph: nothing OK, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come out in an order not stated

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plotting results that show little improvement, someone shrugs that nothing is quite all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progress on a graph' looks like one phrase about a chart, but the definition stops at 'progress'. A learner driver who misuses the clutch makes the car jerk forward this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a car lurching forward in jerks, as a learner driver stalls and restarts, like the bounding marsupial.

clue.text: Was witness to suffer detention?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: to be kept in custody

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the second meaning: to be held is to suffer detention. The question mark flags that split.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the past tense of behold, an old word meaning to see or look upon something directly.

clue.text: Mean to maintain tango beat

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: base means low or mean in character
tango is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for T

explanation.surface: Someone means to keep up the rhythm of a tango.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'mean' a verb of intention and 'beat' a dance rhythm; in fact 'mean' is an adjective and 'beat' a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste someone is an old-fashioned way of saying thrash or give them a sound beating.

clue.text: Bound to miss start after grappling with field event

indicators.note: after places one piece behind what comes before it in the answer

parts.note: a hop is a small bound or leap
to skip a class is to miss it
with gives AND; grappling just says the two are locked together
a jump is a start of surprise

explanation.surface: An athlete wrestling with an event is sure to miss the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'certain to', but 'Bound' is a leap. The field event is the old name for what athletics now calls the triple jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Before it was called the triple jump, this athletics discipline was known by the three movements it involves.

clue.text: See that Carol is down

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look, see that
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: Notice how a girl named Carol is feeling depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name feeling low; it is the verb meaning to sing. Down here means behind in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is down, trailing on the scoreboard, is currently behind its opponents and heading for defeat.

clue.text: A US military hospital losing its second nurse

indicators.note: losing its second means the letter in second place drops out

parts.note: taken as written
MASH stands for Mobile Army Surgical Hospital, famous from the TV series

explanation.surface: A field hospital in the US army runs short of its deputy nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: The hospital's second letter, S, goes. AMAH is a crossword regular from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: In parts of East and South Asia an amah is a nursemaid or domestic servant who looks after children.

clue.text: Political philosopher from US, one men quote erroneously

indicators.note: done erroneously means done wrongly, so the letters are set down in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American thinker is one that men often misquote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From US' reads as an American origin, but it only supplies letters; the thinker was French.
explanation.definitionFit: Montesquieu was the French Enlightenment writer whose Spirit of the Laws set out the separation of powers.

clue.text: Get all outspoken in Rome?

parts.note: all, completely, is wholly
to get a point is to see it

explanation.surface: Visitors to Rome become thoroughly blunt.

explanation.definitionFit: The papacy's jurisdiction and government is often referred to simply by the name of its city, so the two are interchangeable.

clue.text: Ridiculously cheap, fashionable pastry cases from somewhere in Asia

parts.note: filo is a paper-thin pastry
one penny, 1P, is a ridiculously low price

explanation.walkthrough: Read the digit 1 as the letter I: a price of 1P, one penny, is ridiculously cheap. Those letters and IN sit inside the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Filipino is a person or thing belonging to the Philippines, the island nation in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Environmentalists, disapprovingly, to use empty cistern for recycling

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: emptying a word scoops out its middle and leaves only the outer shell

parts.note: only the first and last letters of the word survive

explanation.surface: Green campaigners frown on using an empty water tank to collect material for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disapprovingly' belongs to the definition: it says the answer is a slighting word for green activists.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an econut mocks them as a fanatical, cranky campaigner for the natural world and ecology.

clue.text: Calls round with drink

parts.note: a ring is a round shape
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone pops round with a drink in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls round' looks like a visit, but 'Calls' is the definition and 'round' a ring. The pieces run together across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage, to ring someone up is to telephone them, which is to call them.

clue.text: Bloomer, ultimately encouraging fan to invade pitch

indicators.note: invaders get inside territory, so one piece pushes into the middle of another

parts.note: a sales pitch is a spiel

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A supporter's cheers end with someone running onto the football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or a loaf, but here it is literally something that blooms. Spignel is a rare umbellifer, also called baldmoney or meu.
explanation.definitionFit: Spignel is a flowering plant of mountain grassland, so it is a thing that blooms; the setter uses the word whimsically.

clue.text: King being trapped by horse having reared in southern China

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here between the two parts of the outer phrase

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
china is rhyming slang for mate: china plate
to rear a child is to mother it

explanation.surface: A monarch is caught by a rearing horse while in the south of China.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the horse is the knight. China means friend in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate, mate). 'Having reared' is not the horse rearing up but bringing up young.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess this is a checkmate delivered by a knight when the king is hemmed in by its own pieces and cannot escape.

clue.text: Eccentricity of relatives repeating verses every so often

indicators.note: repeating means saying again, so the same piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: kin are relatives
the same word again

indicators.note: every so often means at regular gaps, so only every other letter is kept

explanation.walkthrough: The relatives are taken twice, then the even letters of the poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinkiness can mean oddness or quirkiness of behaviour, just as eccentricity means departure from the usual.

clue.text: The capital's Circle Line about to be withdrawn

parts.note: an arc is a line forming part of a circle
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here the words describe an arc. The answer is the capital of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa, on the Gulf of Guinea coast.

clue.text: Goddess of the pictures, heading down for cup tie?

parts.note: a semi-final is a cup tie

explanation.surface: A screen goddess, a film star, heads off to watch a football cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pictures' suggests the cinema, but it is art. A cup tie is a knockout match in a British football cup; a semi-final is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis was the Greek goddess of hunting and the moon, twin sister of Apollo.

clue.text: Note short bad-tempered ape used for lab research?

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
cross means bad-tempered
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: A grumpy ape is put to work in a laboratory experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' and 'lab research' suggest animal testing, but the ape is a verb. The definition is cryptic and reads with a question mark: what is used for lab research.

clue.text: Boy requiring uniform collected clothes

uniform is the NATO alphabet word for U

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun for garments, but it is a verb: to clothe is to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Calum is a Scottish male first name, so it is a word for a particular boy.

clue.text: A little blue in demeanour, is querulous

explanation.surface: Someone looking slightly depressed in manner is whining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little blue' suggests sadness, which the surface backs up, but blue here means slightly rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are smutty ones, so mildly blue material is slightly indecent or saucy, which is what risqué means.

clue.text: Those of a certain age, longing to shun society, part with property

parts.note: thirsty means longing, eager
S is the abbreviation for society
some means a part
one's things are one's belongings

clue.text: End of play or film — lute playing

parts.note: the two words taken together

clue.text: Following primitive instincts, turns and twitches?

clue.text: One doing good work first, welcome among factory personnel earlier

clue.text: Proceeds to analyse, first and foremost, one of two books

clue.text: Misbehaving like a competent card player?

clue.text: Porter, not up in Scotland, touring Sandhurst

clue.text: Band leader's tweet to press, backing men

clue.text: Yank's courage

explanation.walkthrough: The capital Y makes it look like an American, but yank is just a sharp pull.

clue.text: Character an old letter once used by mapmakers

clue.text: Light in women's loo wired badly

parts.note: taken as written

taken as written

clue.text: It's a deal that includes reform of Euro

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sporting event must be organised with the computing department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' suggests a contest to be organised with the IT people, but it means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thais are the people of Thailand, an ethnic and national group, so they form a race.

clue.text: Letter from abroad: one to seal well, we understand?

indicators.note: we understand suggests what we have heard said, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: one who seals a well or bottle puts a cap on it

explanation.surface: A letter arrives from overseas from someone who can seal an envelope properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from abroad' sounds like foreign mail, but it is a letter of a foreign alphabet. Said in a British accent the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter used abroad.

clue.text: Palace one's dwelling in deserted, time to move

indicators.note: dwelling in a place means living inside it
this phrase names an abbreviated letter and tells it to change position, so the word's order is altered by one shift

parts.note: a deserted house is vacant; its T is the abbreviation for time
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone lives in an empty palace and it is time to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to move' means the T (time) in the empty word shifts, from the end to third place; then the one goes in after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the official residence of the Pope in Rome, a vast palace complex.

clue.text: Italian constitutional body has boycotted hearing

indicators.note: the body of a word is its middle, and staying away from it leaves only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
audio relates to hearing and sound

explanation.surface: An Italian parliamentary chamber stays away from a public inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional body' looks like one phrase for a parliament, but 'body has boycotted' tells you to drop the middle of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio is an Italian man's first name, so it stands for an Italian, as with Shakespeare's Claudio in Messina and Vienna.

clue.text: Claws: little ones

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the pincers of a crab or lobster
second meaning: British informal for small children

explanation.walkthrough: Nippers is British informal for young children.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a crab's pincers and, informally in Britain, small children.

clue.text: Complete degree

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a position or grade in a hierarchy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete degree' sounds like finishing a university course; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means utter or downright, and as a noun means a level or grade in a scale.

clue.text: Not moving back, I parked behind, between poles

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a state of not moving

indicators.note: between means flanked on either side, so the outer pieces enclose the rest

parts.note: S, south, is a pole, taken twice

indicators.note: behind means following on, so this piece comes after
back means going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a car that has parked has sat in one place
taken as written

explanation.surface: Not reversing, a driver parks behind, wedged between two posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not moving back' reads as one phrase about reversing, but the definition stops at 'moving'. Both poles here are S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a condition of no movement or change, the noun for a state of standing still.

clue.text: Argument with the Italian visiting celebrity: I'm astounded!

parts.note: to have words is to argue

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's home, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: fame is celebrity
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when an Italian drops in on a star, and the onlooker is stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Italian' looks like a person, but it is the Italian word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses being so astonished that one cannot speak, which is what being astounded means.
